<Heading
  as={"h1"}

  children={"Validate a JWT and retrieve user details"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"get"}
  path={"/auth/validate"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Verifies the JWT signature, checks expiry and revocation status, and returns the
decoded token information together with the matching WordPress user profile and roles.

**Audience**
When an expected audience is configured (plugin setting `authorization.aud`, or the
`audience` of the JWT Rule the token matches), the JWT `aud` claim (a string or a list)
must contain it. Otherwise this and every other JWT endpoint answers `401` with
`error_code` 130. JWTs from `/auth`, `/auth/refresh`, register and OAuth carry the
plugin audience when it is set.

**JWT delivery**
The JWT can be passed via:
- `JWT` query parameter
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header (when enabled in plugin General Settings)
- Cookie or session (when enabled in plugin General Settings)

A header, cookie, or session JWT is ignored on cross-site requests (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`,
or an `Origin` / `Referer` naming another site) to prevent CSRF. Cross-origin browser apps must be
listed in the CORS "Allow origin" setting; a `*` entry trusts the header JWT only, never the
cookie or session JWT. Requests without these headers (mobile apps, servers) are not affected.

**Requirements**
- Authentication and the validate endpoint must be enabled in the plugin settings.
- The calling IP must pass the authentication IP allow-list.
- If "Validate Token Requires Auth Code" is enabled, `AUTH_KEY` must be provided.

The response can be changed with the `simple_jwt_login_response_validate_token` filter.
